Early signing period for football close to becoming reality
From Early February to mid-December. Unsurprisingly, SEC objects to a proposed rule change.

It seems most SEC coaches would rather have a post-Thanksgiving signing period. I think getting rid of signing periods all together would be best overall. It would force coaches to be more critical of recruits and think carefully before offering scholarships.
I agree. However,after the Roquan Smith situation last year,I'm also fine with athletes not even having to sign a letter of intent.
What's the Roquan Smith situation? I'm not familiar with what happened.
He flipped from UCLA after their DC left. Went to Georgia, broke his letter of intent, post-signing day.
Oh yeah I can see that. I agree that if a coach recruits a kid and then the coach leaves, the kid shouldn't be bound by his letter of intent.

Roquan Smith committed to UCLA on the morning on national signing day after being split 50/50 between Georgia and UCLA. Prior to his commitment rumors began circulating that Ulbricht, his position coach and primary recruiter at UCLA, had taken a job as DC of the Atlanta Falcons. UGA coaches informed Roquan of this before he faxed in his LOI. With this information, Roquan placed his commitment on hold until he had more information. Long story short, Roquan decided that it was in his best interests to stick with his heart and attend UGA. However, he did not sign a LOI. He's now enrolled in classes at UGA.
Why sign the letter if you dont have to? Tell them you will be there and show up.
